text:
Maria: Heads-up — opened a PR to change admission control behavior in us-west. Proposal: switch from hard reject at capacity to a soft-deny (degrade) path + short warm queue for bursty jobs. Need quick feedback before EOD.

Leo: Can you outline the exact behavior? soft-deny = still serve but at lower quality? queue = how long?

Maria: Short version: when pool_util >= 90% we: 1) prefer degrade variants (shorter max_tokens, lower quant model) 2) allow a tiny in-memory queue (default 3s) for requests that look batchable 3) only start 503s after queue+degrade exhausted.

Anya: Concern: fairness. If we always degrade instead of rejecting, noisy tenants could eat up GPU cycles even if degraded. How do we protect SLO customers?

Maria: Good point. PR includes priority tiers. Reserved/paid tenants skip degrade until 95% and get prefetched warm slots. Free tier hits degrade first. Also token caps per-request when degraded.

Shawn: What about tail latency? If we queue for 3s then degrade, p99 could spike. Any telemetry or sim results?

Maria: Ran a weekend sim with production trace. With 3s queue + degrade we saw median latency +5ms, p95 +40ms, p99 +220ms vs hard reject which had p99 constant but more 503s. I put the sim graphs in the PR description.

Kevin: Cross-region routing cost: if we prefer to route to eu-west fallback, network egress and cross-region cold caches will blow up cost and latency. Can we prefer warm replicas before cross-region?

Maria: Yes — routing priority: local warm pool -> local degrade variants -> local small queue -> regional warm replica -> hard reject. I added a config param route_preference in the PR so SRE/product can tune per-customer.

ops-bot: Metric snapshot: us-west gpu_pool_util 10m_avg=92%, active_queues=37, avg_queue_time=2.1s, degrade_ratio=0.12

Anya: Also think about KV cache churn if we degrade model size. If we frequently swap quant/arch variants, KV cold misses will increase token compute. Need a cost model in PR.

Maria: Agreed — added a cost calc section. Degrade is cheaper per-token but has higher cold-starts; net wins for short bursts, loses for long sustained saturation. We're gating degrade for >30s sustained windows.

Shawn: Suggest experiment: A/B for 24h with 5% traffic on soft-deny + warm-queue config vs baseline rejects. Track p99 latency, 503 rate, cost delta, customer error rate.

Leo: SGTM. Also add alerting: if p99 > 2s or 503s > baseline by +0.5% for 15m, rollback.

deploy-bot: Canary plan created: eng-infra/canary/admit-soft-deny-2026-03-18, rollout 5% -> 25% -> 100% w/ 30m pauses.

Maria: Action items: (1) land PR with canary flags (I will), (2) SRE to monitor p99+503s (Shawn/Anya), (3) Product to sign off on tiered behavior (Kevin), (4) Ops to review cross-region routing cost calc (Kevin). I'll ping everyone when canary starts. :thumbsup:

Kevin: Will review cost calc today. If we see >15% egress bump we should fallback to reject for free-tier only.

Anya: I'll wire up the alerts and dashboard queries. Expect PR comments in next hour.

Maria: Thanks team — appreciate quick eyes.
